samples.summary: `cloneTableCells` does not clone or re-id nested `tableData`, so the cell paste this delta hardens still writes duplicate block ids and aliases the clipboard payload into the document
samples.evidence: `cloneTableCells` (clipboard.ts:503-517) spreads each block (`{...b, id: generateBlockId(), inlines, style}`) but never recurses into `b.tableData`. The delta's premise is explicitly that "a clipboard cell may carry a whole nested table of its own" (text-editor.ts:4699) and `pasteTableCells` clones each cell with this helper (text-editor.ts:4731, 4766). Two consequences on that exact path: (a) every block inside the nested table keeps its ORIGINAL id, so an internal copy/paste of a cell containing a nested table inserts blocks whose ids already exist in the same document — `blockParentMap`, `doc.findBlock`, `resolveBlockTreePath` and cursor placement are all keyed by block id, so the duplicated ids resolve to the wrong node; (b) the pasted cell's `tableData` object is the same object as the parsed clipboard payload's, and the new `capTableCellsNesting` now mutates it in place (`cell.blocks = capTableNesting(...)`, clipboard.ts:468, recursing into `cell.blocks = ...` at clipboard.ts:440), so the document ends up holding a structure the paste code also mutated as "clipboard data". The cap work the delta adds is correct only for the top level of each cell; the shallow clone under it is what actually reaches the CRDT.

samples.summary: `insertTableRow`/`insertTableColumn` still write rows/cells at or past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, creating exactly the "rows nobody can read" state the new refusal then makes permanent (the block becomes unwritable forever)
samples.evidence: `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2933-2948) and `insertTableColumn` (2966-2990) build `buildRowNode(row, rowDepth)` / `buildCellNode(cells[r], rowDepth)` with no check that `rowDepth < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, unlike `buildBlockNode` (386-402), which truncates at the cap, and unlike `Doc.insertTableInCell` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:925), which refuses. The PR's own test constructs the hazardous state with precisely this writer (`store.insertTableRow(atCap.id, 0, ...)` in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts's `peerRowsPastTheCap`). Once those rows exist, the new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` makes every `updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` over the enclosing subtree throw (1833, 3021) — the subtree is permanently uneditable by every replica, not just refused once. Also note `insertTableRow` then splices the row into a model whose table read back as `rows: []`, so the local cache and any fresh read disagree immediately.
searchedFor: grep MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH across packages/frontend and packages/docs

samples.summary: `pasteTableCells` derives its cap depth from a different parent map than the one it uses to decide it is in a cell; if they disagree the new cap silently becomes a no-op (or over-drops)
samples.evidence: Line 4714 reads `cellInfo` from `layout.blockParentMap` (the layout just returned by `this.getLayout()`), while line 4719-4720 reads the depth from `this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId)`, which walks `Doc._blockParentMap` — a separately-maintained merged map written only in editor.ts:1704 (and text-box-editor.ts:479). If the doc map lacks `pos.blockId` while the layout map has it, `cellBaseDepth` is 0 and `capTableNesting` early-returns the blocks untouched (`if (baseDepth <= 0) return blocks;`, clipboard.ts:430) — the whole new ceiling is bypassed for that paste. The mirror case (doc map deeper than the layout map, `cellInfo` undefined) yields `depth + 1` and silently drops tables that would have been legal. `insertBlocks` has the same coupling, but this call adds a `+ (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)` term that assumes the two maps agree.

samples.summary: `Math.max(1, ...cells.map(r => r.length))` in the rewritten `pasteTableCells` can throw `RangeError` on a large clipboard payload — the same hazard `normalizeCellRange` deliberately folds around
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:4725 spreads one argument per clipboard row into `Math.max`; past roughly 100k arguments V8 throws `RangeError: too many arguments`. `deserializeClipboard`/`sanitizeCellRows` (clipboard.ts:496) caps nesting depth but no row count, and the payload is attacker-supplied per the file's own comment (clipboard.ts:493). selection.ts:210-214 explicitly avoids the identical spread for exactly this reason ("`Math.max(...rows)` throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments"). A throw here aborts the paste batch rather than corrupting data, hence minor.

samples.summary: The new `updateBlock` refusal throws on a path whose callers have already mutated the in-memory model; outside a `batch()` nothing rolls that back
samples.evidence: `updateBlock` now throws before `withUpdate` (1833-1835). Callers in packages/docs mutate the block object obtained from the live cached document and only then call the store — e.g. `pasteTableCells` mutates `td.rows[...]` and `normalizeTableMerges(td)` before `this.doc.updateBlockDirect(tableBlockId, tableBlock)` (text-editor.ts:4769-4775), and `Doc.updateBlockDirect` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:793-796) calls `this.refresh()` only AFTER a successful store write. Inside `doc.batch` the throw is recovered (`Doc.batch` refreshes, document.ts:198-205, and the store nulls `cachedDoc`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3322-3324), but `updateBlockDirect` is also reachable outside a batch, where `Doc._document` keeps the mutation the CRDT never received and the editor renders state no replica holds. No caller anywhere catches this error (grep for catch under packages/frontend/src/app/docs shows none around store writes).

The delta's premise is explicitly that "a clipboard cell may carry a whole nested table of its own" (text-editor.ts:4699) and `pasteTableCells` clones each cell with this helper (text-editor.ts:4731, 4766). verdict.reason: The shallow-clone itself exists as described (clipboard.ts:509-514 spreads `...b`, so `tableData` is shared and nested ids are not regenerated), but both blocking consequences the finding rests on are already prevented. (a) Duplicate ids: the only production source of cells carrying a nested `tableData` into `pasteTableCells` is `deserializeClipboard` (text-editor.ts:1747 -> 1753-1758 -> 1575 -> pasteTableCells:4706), and `sanitizeBlock` regenerates EVERY block id, recursing into nested tables via `sanitizeTableData` -> `sanitizeCell(depth+1)` -> `sanitizeBlocks` -> `sanitizeBlock` (clipboard.ts:363-366, 319, 287, 405-412). So nested blocks arrive with ids already freshly generated, never the source document's, and cannot collide with live ids. The other two cell sources (`parseHtmlTableToTableCells` clipboard.ts:917, `parseMarkdownTableToTableCells` clipboard.ts:1033) build cells through `makeCellFromInlines`, which also calls `generateBlockId()` (clipboard.ts:847-857). (b) Aliasing: the parsed payload is a transient local inside the `runPaste` job closure (text-editor.ts:1735, 1746-1760), re-parsed per paste event and retained by nothing; each source cell is cloned into exactly one target (text-editor.ts:4728-4736, 4757-4771), so no two document cells share a `tableData` and `capTableCellsNesting`'s in-place mutation of the shared object has no observable effect after the paste. The copy/cut sites (1436, 1479) only `JSON.stringify` the aliased clone, and in `handleCut` serialization (1480-1482) precedes `deleteSelection()` (1484). The shallowness is latent fragility, not a firing defect on any reachable path.

verdict.reason: The reviewer's evidence checks out line-for-line. `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2933-2948) computes `rowDepth` via `resolveTableRowDepth` and passes it straight to `buildRowNode(row, rowDepth)` (2935) with no comparison against MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH and no `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` call; `insertTableColumn` (2966-2990) does the same with `buildCellNode(cells[r], rowDepth)` (2978). `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` (433-439, 425-431) only forward depth to `buildBlockNode`, which caps *nested* tables (398) but never suppresses the row/cell node itself, so a row written under a table already at/past the cap lands in the CRDT as rows no reader will ever return (`treeNodeToBlock` truncates at 575). That is precisely the state `treeHasTruncatedRows` (485-500) detects, and once it exists the new refusals in `updateBlock` (1833-1835) and `updateTableCell` (3021-3026) throw for every replica over the enclosing subtree — a permanently unwritable region, plus an immediate cache/tree divergence from the `rows.splice` at 2945/2986 into a table the reader handed back as `rows: []`. I searched for a guard on every hop and found none: `Doc.insertRow`/`insertColumn` (document.ts:999-1014, 1048-1064) check nothing, their callers `editor.insertTableRow/insertTableColumn` (editor.ts:4314-4350) and text-editor.ts:6020 gate only on `blockParentMap`, `memory.ts:346/358` is uncapped, and the repo-wide MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH sites (clipboard.ts:437, docx-importer.ts:437, docs-tree.ts:179/237, docs-content.controller.ts:454, table-layout.ts:145, editor.ts:4232, document.ts:925) all guard other writers, none of them this one. The PR's own test constructs the hazard with this exact writer (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3790). Caveat recorded for weighting, not refutation: I could not find a UI path that reaches it, since an at-cap table reads as `rows: []` and therefore contributes no cell to `blockParentMap`, so reach appears to be direct store/`Doc` callers — that argues the severity is contained, but the missing cap and the resulting permanent-refusal state are real.

finding.summary: The "refuse rather than replicate a read-time truncation" guard lives only in `writeFullDocument`; every incremental writer happily writes the truncated model back, deleting a peer's rows
finding.evidence:
`writeFullDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3330-3352) refuses a document containing a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, on the stated grounds that `getDocument()` truncated that table to `rows: []` and rewriting it would turn a read-time truncation into a replicated deletion. But the same truncated model reaches the CRDT through writers that carry no such refusal:
- `updateBlock` → `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block, this.blockPathNestingDepth(...)))` (~line 1750): if `block` is the table read at the cap, `buildBlockNode` is called with `depth >= MAX` and emits `children: []`, replacing the peer's rows in the tree with nothing.
- `updateTableCell` (~line 2924) → `buildCellNode(cell, rowDepth)` — same, for every nested table inside the rewritten cell.
- `insertTableRow` / `insertTableColumn` (~2841/2874) and `insertBlockAfter`/`insertBlocksAfter`.
- `setHeader` / `setFooter` tree paths (lines 968-985, 1007-1026) rewrite the whole header/footer node from `getDocument()`'s truncated blocks via `buildBlockNode(b, 0)` with no cap check at all.
So the refusal binds only the one path that already had no realistic caller, while the ordinary edit paths do exactly the destructive thing it was added to prevent. (Backend `writeDocsRoot` has the same guard and no incremental twin, so the hole is frontend-side.)

verdict.reason: The claimed hole does not exist. The refusal is not confined to `writeFullDocument`: the repository has a shared private helper `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1748-1753) built on `treeHasTruncatedRows`/`truncatedRowsError` (:485-509), and every replacing incremental writer named in the finding calls it. `updateBlock` gates the `editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block, blockDepth))` at :1847 with `if (hasTableAtNestingCap([block], blockDepth)) assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows(blockPath, blockDepth)` at :1833-1835. `updateTableCell` does the same at :3021-3026 before `buildCellNode(cell, rowDepth)` at :3027. `setHeader` and `setFooter`, which the finding says have "no cap check at all", check at :1015-1017 and :1060-1063 respectively, before rewriting the header/footer node from `getDocument()`'s blocks. The remaining writers cited (`insertTableRow` :2941, `insertTableColumn` :2975-2979, `insertBlockAfter` :2463-2467, `insertBlocksAfter` :2514) all issue edits whose start path equals their end path, i.e. pure inserts that overwrite no existing node and therefore cannot delete a peer's rows; their at-cap degradation to a rowless table applies only to newly supplied content and is the documented intent (:467-479). Tests at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3797-3826 assert precisely the refusals the finding claims are absent, with the peer's row still in the tree afterward. The finding's own line numbers are additionally ~100 off from the real code (writeFullDocument is at :3429, not 3330-3352).
